hook: Their nest is a tree that takes a century to grow.
caption:
Their nest is a tree that takes a century to grow.

Most temperate-forest owls do not build nests at all; they nest in cavities, hollows that form when a major branch breaks off a mature tree and decay slowly excavates the heartwood, a process that takes between eighty and two hundred years depending on the species. The Spotted Owl, Great Gray Owl, and Boreal Owl all require this kind of tree to breed, and the kind of tree that produces it is the kind logging companies want most. Industrial timber rotations cut at sixty to eighty years, before any cavity has formed, and across the Pacific Northwest old-growth forest now covers under fifteen percent of its pre-1850 range. A nest cavity cannot be replaced inside a human lifetime, and the owls that need them cannot wait.
